title: Reconcile the portable-paths scan set with what exists on disk
action: Per E3, scripts/tests/test_portable_paths.mjs:23-34 builds its scan set from `git ls-files -z` -- the git INDEX -- with no existence filter. Its sibling test_doctrine_parity.mjs:136 already carries exactly the filter this needs, added after the same defect made THAT suite crash on ENOENT. This one does not crash only because its loop analyses path strings and never touches the filesystem, so the bug is the quiet direction: the index omits untracked-but-real files, so a staged-but-unindexed file with an illegal Windows character sails through green. Two changes: add the existence filter, and union the listing with `git status --porcelain` so untracked reality is covered -- follow the shape already used by gitImpactedFiles()/statusPorcelainFiles() at scripts/run_verify.mjs:875-909 rather than inventing a second approach. Prove the fix with a real case: a file present on disk but absent from the index must now be scanned. Capture the before state from the current code, author no probe script.

truths: A path present on disk but absent from the git index is included in the scan set
A path in the index but deleted from disk is excluded

artifacts.substantive: scan set filtered by existence and unioned with porcelain status

key_links: the union follows run_verify.mjs's existing porcelain helper shape, not a second implementation
prohibitions: No weakening of the portable-path assertions themselves

trace.outcome: Added existence filter + git-status-porcelain union to test_portable_paths.mjs's scan set, matching test_doctrine_parity.mjs's pattern; proved with a real untracked illegal-named file (before: silent PASS, after: correct FAIL) and an isolated-repo indexed-but-deleted case (correctly excluded, PASS 0).
